lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: identifying who helps with what

objective: Learners map, in general role terms, who could help with different parts of their transition, matching each part of the plan to a role (such as a school counselor, a guardian, a mentor, or a peer), without needing to name specific real people if they would rather keep the map general.
scenario: Using a list of transition plan parts (paperwork and deadlines, financial questions, day-to-day check-ins, emotional support, and logistics such as housing or transportation), the learner matches each part to a role that could help with it, optionally naming a specific person but always free to keep any entry at the role level.
safetyNotes: The learner is never required to name a specific real person; a role-level answer (such as 'a school counselor' or 'a mentor') is a complete and acceptable response for every entry.
materials: the provided list of transition plan parts
paper or a document for the learner's own map

tasks.directions: Before mapping, think about the roles available to you in general.

prompts.text: Without naming anyone specifically yet, what kinds of roles (school staff, household members, mentors, peers, community contacts) do you have some access to right now?

tasks.directions: For each part of the transition plan listed, match it to a role that could realistically help, using the example provided as a model.

prompts.text: I matched at least four different parts of the transition plan to a role that could help with each.
For one part of the plan, explain briefly why that particular role is the right fit for that kind of help.

tasks.directions: Complete your own role-support map for the full plan, keeping entries at the role level unless you would rather name a specific person.

prompts.text: Write your completed role-support map, listing each plan part and the role assigned to it. You may name a specific person for any entry, or keep it at the role level — both are complete answers.

tasks.directions: Reflect on any gaps in your map.

prompts.text: Is there any part of your plan with no role assigned yet, and if so, what kind of role would need to fill that gap?

remediation: If a learner leaves multiple plan parts unmatched or assigns the same single role to everything, reteach by walking through one plan part at a time and asking specifically what kind of help it requires (paperwork help looks different from emotional support), then matching a distinct role to each.
extension: Have the learner identify one role in their map that is not yet confirmed or contacted, and write a plain, one-line way they could check whether that role is actually available to help.
